title: Python Collections Overview
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Computer Science
description: Interactive p5.js 2x2 matrix that organizes Python's list, tuple, set, and frozenset by ordered vs unordered and mutable vs immutable, with hover details, expandable code examples, and a 12-question classification quiz.

learningObjectives: Classify Python's four core collection types (list, tuple, set, frozenset) by whether they are ordered and whether they are mutable.
Compare the types on duplicates, indexing, and use as a dictionary key.
Select the appropriate collection type for a given scenario and justify the choice.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification on a 2x2 matrix with hover comparison, worked code examples, and a quiz with hints and retry
keyQuestions: Does this collection keep its items in order?
Can this collection change after it is created?
Why can a tuple or a frozenset be a dictionary key when a list or a set cannot?
commonMisconceptions: Tuples are just lists with different brackets
Sets keep items in the order you added them
Any collection can be used as a dictionary key
assessmentOpportunities: First-try score on the 12-question classification quiz
Students invent a scenario and justify which quadrant it belongs in
